subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Transformers: Stepping Voltage Up and Down
description: One-minute skill: Transformers: Stepping Voltage Up and Down.

hook.text: Power leaves a plant at 400,000 volts and arrives at your outlet at 120 or 240. Transformers make that possible.

buildup.text: A transformer has two coils around an iron core. The turns ratio determines voltage change. More turns means more voltage.

discovery.text: Step-up transformers increase voltage for transmission. Step-down transformers reduce it for homes. Same device, different ratios.

twist.text: Transformers only work with AC. That's why Edison's DC system couldn't compete — no way to change voltage efficiently.

climax.text: Modern transformers exceed 99% efficiency. Almost no energy is lost in the conversion process.

punchline.text: Two coils. One core. Voltage goes up or down on demand.

quiz.question: Why can't transformers work with DC power?
options: DC voltage is too low for the coils to generate a magnetic field
Transformers need a changing magnetic field, which only AC provides
DC current would melt the iron core due to excessive heat
